text:
**For most people, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** Nearly all the sources agree on this.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000-6,000 cycles, versus roughly 500-1,000 for NMC. For daily use, such as a van or a solar cabin, that is about 8 years versus 1.5-3 years ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells failed more mildly (lower peak temperature, smoke without flames), while the NMC cells ignited. LFP isn't fireproof, though, and one study found LFP reached thermal runaway sooner in overcharge ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Cost:** The price gap has mostly closed. One retailer's data shows a median of $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Per rated cycle, LFP is far cheaper.
- **Availability:** In OutageMath's database, 48 of 54 models are LFP, and most NMC models are legacy.

**Where NMC still has an edge**
- **Weight:** NMC cells hold more energy per kilogram, but finished stations show a smaller gap. OutageMath found only about 10% more Wh per pound for the median NMC model. Some LFP stations are lighter per Wh than some NMC ones, so compare actual specs.
- **Light or occasional use:** If you'll cycle it only 30-50 times a year, or only for rare outages, NMC's cycle rating won't be the limit. Choose on weight and price instead ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Cold weather:** This is mostly a wash. Most stations of either chemistry won't charge below 32°F, so check each model's manual ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Rule of thumb**
- Daily use, indoor or vehicle storage, or home backup: LiFePO4.
- Weight-critical, light use, or a deeply discounted NMC unit you'll rarely cycle: NMC can work.
- Always check the spec sheet for the chemistry and for a cycle rating with its end point (80% vs 70%).

**An LFP example:** the [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station rated for 6,000+ cycles to 80%, with a 2,600 W inverter and a 5-year warranty. It lists at $899 and isn't expandable, so it suits home outage backup rather than a system you plan to grow. I didn't follow them, so I'm just citing it for the specs and price. Check the price at the official store before buying.
